analysis: The trial executed successfully but reduced host validation macro HR@10 to 0.4275, down 0.0563 from the current reference (0.4838) and 0.1037 from the historical best (0.5312). Category HR@10: Movies_and_TV 0.465, Industrial_and_Scientific 0.495, Electronics 0.340, CDs_and_Vinyl 0.410. Untying input and retrieval embeddings did not improve this configuration. Reduced parameter sharing may weaken sparse-item learning, but the reported results do not establish the cause. Allocated GPU time was 368.635 seconds; no test results were used.
code_summary: One independently trained SASRec per category, loading one selected checkpoint for prediction. Each network uses 96-dimensional embeddings, two causal Transformer blocks, two attention heads, dropout 0.3, absolute positions, and learned bucketed relative-position biases. Separate output embeddings are initialized by copying input embeddings without additional random draws, then trained jointly. Positive, negative, and inference scores use output embeddings plus learned item bias. Training retains 2,048 sampled negatives, a 2,048-token cap, endpoint-weighted cross-entropy, AdamW, and seed 42. The predictor imports the same architecture, validates metadata, strictly loads checkpoints, and preserves all four dataset routes. Reload score-agreement assertions are included.
